fields.meta_title: Short-Form Landing Page Builder With Examples | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A short-form landing page keeps the copy brief and the form to one or two fields. See four examples, then build one that saves each signup.
fields.h1: Build a Short-Form Landing Page With Two Fields or Fewer
fields.hero_description: Build a short-form landing page that states the offer in a few lines and saves each signup to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Short Page Still Needs Behind It
fields.features_subheading: The visitor sees a headline and a small form. Six parts behind the page decide what each signup sets off.
fields.feature_1:
The page and its form from one prompt

Describe the offer and the one or two details you need from each visitor. Emergent builds the page and the signup table behind it, then changes either one when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
Every signup saved as a row you own

Each submission lands as a row in a database you own, stamped with the time it arrived and the page it came from. Sort the rows by date, or filter them to a single offer.
fields.feature_3:
A callback request sent to one person

Name who answers each request, such as a dispatcher for quote calls. That person gets an email, a Slack message, or an in-app alert with the name and number the visitor typed.
fields.feature_4:
New emails copied to your mailing list

Your email platform receives each new address as it arrives, as long as it has an API. The welcome series you already run starts from there, with no export or upload in between.
fields.feature_5:
A longer version for the same offer

Ask for a second page that tells the full story, with reviews and answers to common doubts. Both versions write to one table, and each row records the version its signup came from.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and the code on paid plans

Publish on a custom domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the page, its form, and its signup table to your own GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
One email field, then BREAD15 on the screen

Pell Street Bakery's page offers 15% off a first order in one line, above a single email field. Once the email is saved, the code BREAD15 appears where the form was. This month, 214 signups landed in the bakery's table, each one stamped with the day it came in.
fields.tab_content_2:
When a trial lists 25 students or more, it is tagged Team plan

Teachers who try Slatebook, a scheduling app for tutors, answer two questions to start the 14-day trial: a work email and the number of students they teach. Each signup becomes a row in the trial table. Rows with 25 students or more carry the Team plan tag, and the rest are tagged Solo.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each callback request lands with Marisol Okafor

When someone asks Northbay Movers for a moving quote, the page takes a name and a phone number and nothing more. Dispatcher Marisol Okafor gets an email with both as soon as the form is sent, and she calls back within 15 minutes. Room counts and moving dates come up on that call, not on the page.
fields.tab_content_4:
With 140 words, the page drew 118 signups to 79

In March, Carraway Language Studio offered a free trial lesson on two pages that asked for the same two fields: a name and an email. One page ran 140 words, the other 1,100. Each got 1,800 visitors, and every signup was saved with the version it came from. The short page took 118 signups and the long one 79.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Short-Form Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to keep a short-form landing page to the few lines and fields its offer needs, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Match the length to the offer
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the offer in the headline
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Cut every field the reply can skip
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Keep the form on the first screen
fields.howto_step_1_des: Instapage's guide to page length puts it plainly: the more expensive the offer, the more copy you need to explain why visitors should convert. Keep the short format for free or low-cost offers, such as a discount code or a callback.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write what the visitor gets, with its terms, as the headline itself: "15% off your first order" says more than a welcome line. If the offer cannot stand without a paragraph of explanation, it belongs on a longer page instead.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Nielsen Norman Group advises removing fields whose information can be derived some other way, collected more conveniently later, or left out. On a short page, that can leave a single email field, or a name and a number to call back.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Open the page on a phone before launch. The headline and the button should both show without scrolling. If a photo pushes the button out of view, shrink the photo or cut it, and check the phone view again.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Match the ad that sent the visitor
fields.howto_step_5_des: Reuse the words of the ad or email that links to the page, especially the offer and the price. A visitor who clicked for a free trial lesson should see those words first, not a general welcome to the school.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Take off the site menu and any second offer. A short page has room for one button, and each extra link gives the visitor a way to leave before the form. The logo can stay, unlinked.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run a longer version beside it
fields.howto_step_7_des: Build a longer page for the same offer and send each one a similar share of visitors from the same source. Compare signups per visitor, not raw counts, and wait until both pages have a few hundred visits before you choose.

faq_plan.q: What is a short-form landing page?
faq_plan.a: A short-form landing page is a standalone page that makes one offer in a handful of lines, then asks for one or two details, such as an email address. Instapage's guide says these pages tell a simple story, and they do so quickly. A long-form page makes its case at length before the form appears.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a short-form landing page?
faq_plan.a: Choose one offer and the fewest fields that let you follow up. Then describe both to Emergent's AI landing page builder, for example a page for a free trial lesson that asks for a name and an email. It writes the copy and creates the table every signup is saved to, and you publish when the page reads right.

faq_plan.q: When should I use a short-form landing page instead of a long one?
faq_plan.a: Use the short format when the visitor already knows what the offer is and it costs little or nothing, such as a coupon or a callback. Choose the long one when the visitor needs proof or answers before filling in anything. Emergent builds either version from a plain-English prompt and changes it by prompting.

faq_plan.q: How many words should a short-form landing page have?
faq_plan.a: Aim for a page a visitor can read in under a minute: a headline, a line or two of detail, and the form. The trial lesson example on this page ran 140 words. A minimalist landing page goes further and strips back the design as well, while a short page can keep its photos and color.

faq_plan.q: How many form fields should a short-form landing page ask for?
faq_plan.a: One or two. Ask only for what the next step needs: an email to send a code to, or a phone number to call. Nielsen Norman Group's form advice states that every time you cut a field from a form, you increase its conversion rate. Ask for the rest once you have replied.

faq_plan.q: What should a short-form landing page show after someone signs up?
faq_plan.a: Show the result right away, on the same screen if you can: the discount code or the time to expect a call. Replace the form with the code or the call time. The changed screen is the confirmation. Emergent builds that confirmation step from the same plain-English prompt as the page.

faq_plan.q: Should a short-form landing page open its form from a button?
faq_plan.a: No, put the form on the page itself. A button that opens the form on a second screen adds a step to an offer that needs only one or two fields. That two-step layout is a click through landing page, and it suits offers that need explaining before the visitor is asked for anything.

faq_plan.q: How do I test a short-form landing page against a longer version?
faq_plan.a: Keep everything but the length the same: the headline and the fields. If the long page also adds a field, you cannot tell which change moved the result. Instapage's guide on page length recommends A/B testing, because every offer is different.

faq_plan.q: Should a short-form landing page include customer reviews?
faq_plan.a: Yes, one short review or a star rating fits under the button without making the page long. Pick proof that answers the visitor's one doubt about this offer, such as a line about the bread on a bakery discount. Emergent changes the page by prompting, and a new review takes one sentence to swap in.

faq_plan.q: Can a short-form landing page include a video?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the clip is short and sits beside the form instead of above it. Keep the email field in view while the video plays, and a visitor can sign up without watching to the end. When the video carries the whole pitch, build a video landing page instead, with the form under the player.
